answer: Vine-Consistent Voyage Ledger Each agent must maintain a continuous, cryptographically signed record of its past actions—its voyage—anchored to a shared basalt chain. To join or act in a new epoch, an agent must prove its current identity matches a valid path from a prior epoch’s state, verified via Merkle proofs rooted in the basalt ledger. The vine of prior behavior must not fork; any deviation invalidates the agent. An attacker cloning identities cannot replicate the full historical journey required, as each prior action must be re-executed under the same cryptographic key.
